## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (eleven suggestion-level findings, none at or above the critical threshold)

The pull request is ready to merge: every one of the seventy-one checklist items passed, all eleven acceptance criteria are itemized and verified against the shipped code, and no reviewer raised a critical or important defect — what remains is documentation precision, type-design advice, and one test-coverage gap, none of which changes behavior.

Rule applied: rule 6 — a finding below the threshold remains → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (11)

<details>
<summary>11 items</summary>

1. The docstring of `stream_request` in `src/sqllens/agent/integrations/anthropic/llm.py` (line 105) still promises "Yields text chunks as they arrive", while the rewritten body drains the whole `text_stream` inside one `asyncio.to_thread` call at line 124 and only then yields every chunk in the loop at line 126; the inline comment at lines 112-118 describes the new behavior correctly, so the docstring and the comment two lines apart contradict each other. Reported in earlier iterations with no fix decision recorded, and still present at this head. (raised by 2/4 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: no mechanism's covered set is in dispute, and making the sentence true would change no output or branch; searched the repository for the literal "Yields text chunks" and for readers of this docstring across .sh, .py, .yml, .yaml, .jq, .toml and .cfg files and found only llm.py itself; the docstring belongs to a vendored source module the program never prints, so no reader outside the repository sees it -->
2. The docstring of `truncate_messages` in `src/sqllens/conversation_store.py` (lines 109-114) tells the reader that returning `False` "is never an error", but the user-id mismatch branch at line 119 differs in kind from the other two: the conversation still exists and still holds the cancelled call's messages, which is the same consequence that the sibling missing-seam arm in `src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py` logs at ERROR. Neither the returned `bool` nor the caller's single INFO line ("nothing to roll back (unknown/evicted id, or already at %d message(s))") lets the three outcomes be told apart. The branch is unreachable with the shipped single-user `_StaticUserResolver`, so it is behavior-inert today. (raised by 2/4 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: the finding disputes the wording of a docstring rather than the set of inputs any guard covers, and correcting it changes no branch; searched the repository for the literal "never an error" and found only an unrelated comment at .github/workflows/ci.yml line 203, which reads nothing in conversation_store.py; the docstring lives in a source file the program never prints -->
3. Rollback leaves `updated_at` describing a turn whose messages are gone: `src/sqllens/conversation_store.py` line 123 deletes the message tail with `del conversation.messages[length:]` from outside the model, while `Conversation.add_message` stamps `updated_at` alongside every append. After a cancel rollback the conversation's `updated_at` still reflects the cancelled turn, and that field is the sort key used by `list_conversations` at line 90, so the invariant "`updated_at` is the time of the newest message" is enforced for appends and bypassed for removals. (raised by 2/4 agents)
4. The comment blocks added to `src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py` (lines 213-236, 251-259 and 425-434, with the same shape at lines 114-122 and 155-171) spend most of their length on provenance and reachability analysis rather than on the wrong edit a maintainer might otherwise make: the `_rollback_conversation` docstring runs about twenty lines on why the store attribute is unguarded and why the code logs at ERROR rather than raising, when the load-bearing instruction is the single sentence "must not suspend; do not `await` here", and lines 251-259 and 425-434 mostly record that a branch is unreachable with the default wiring. The run-in-executor comments in the three runners and in `runtime.py` are the right shape by contrast: one named wrong change and one named consequence. (raised by 1/4 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: the finding is about the length and subject of comment prose, not about what any mechanism covers, and rewriting it changes no output; searched the repository for tools or agent-instruction files reading these comments across .sh, .py, .yml, .yaml, .jq, .toml and .cfg files and found none; the comments sit in a source module the program never prints -->
5. `_ConversationQueueEntry` in `src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py` (lines 113-126) is anemic: its invariant — `users` equals the number of calls holding or awaiting `lock`, and the entry exists in `_CONVERSATION_QUEUES` exactly while `users > 0` — is maintained by hand at three separate sites (the increment at line 179, the dict registration at lines 175-178, and the decrement inside `_release_queue_entry` at line 149), and `users` is a public mutable `int` with no acquire or release behavior on the type. `_release_queue_entry` line 150 tests `users <= 0` rather than `== 0`, folding a future double release into the same branch as the correct zero case, so such a release would delete a still-live entry silently. Behavior on the paths this change ships is correct. (raised by 1/4 agents)
6. The store seam the change depends on is expressed in no type: `truncate_messages` is declared only on `BoundedConversationStore` (`src/sqllens/conversation_store.py` lines 93-124) while the `ConversationStore` base class declares only asynchronous methods, so the production caller probes with `getattr(store, "truncate_messages", None)` and degrades to an ERROR log (`src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py` lines 236-247), and both helper signatures type the dependency as `agent: Any` (lines 195-197 and 213-215), which leaves a type checker unable to see the required `conversation_store` and `user_resolver` pair or a typo in either attribute name. (raised by 1/4 agents)
7. `truncate_messages` takes a raw `user_id: str` (`src/sqllens/conversation_store.py` lines 93-95, compared at line 119) while every sibling — `get_conversation`, `delete_conversation` and `list_conversations` at lines 63-91 — takes a `User` and unwraps the identity itself, so the one method that can delete data is the one whose caller is trusted to have unwrapped it, and an unrelated string is a well-typed argument that matches no conversation and returns `False` as a silently skipped rollback. The caller makes that shape reachable: `src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py` lines 422-423 initialize `baseline_user_id = ""` and `baseline_messages = 0` as independent locals with the empty string standing for "no baseline", kept out of the call only by the `queued_id is not None` guard at line 456. The `length < 0` precondition is raised explicitly at line 117 while this identity precondition is not. (raised by 1/4 agents)
8. `_conversation_turn` in `src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py` (lines 154-192) encodes two independent decisions in one `str | None` yield — which conversation id to roll back, and whether a turn lock was taken — and the caller at lines 422-457 re-derives the baseline pair from two separately initialized locals, so the illegal combinations (locked with no baseline, baseline with no lock) are prevented by a guard rather than made unrepresentable by a type. (raised by 1/4 agents)
9. The health-check clause added to `docs/external/getting-started.md` (line 57) asserts "so its health check keeps answering", but `/healthz` exists only in the HTTP transport's path normalizer (`src/sqllens/transport/http.py`), while the same paragraph walks the reader through stdio mode as the recommended setup for Claude Desktop on macOS, where there is no health endpoint. The acceptance criterion asks only for the "does not stop the server from accepting other requests" half, which the sentence already carries. Reported earlier with no fix decision; still present. (raised by 1/4 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=not-held; evidence: the finding disputes one sentence's scope rather than the inputs any guard covers, and deleting the clause changes no program output; searched the repository for the literal "health check keeps answering" and for consumers of this page across .sh, .py, .yml, .yaml, .jq, .toml and .cfg files and found only the page itself; the page is published external documentation, so limb two fails and the cap is 🟠 Important, weighed at the lower of that and the finding's own 🟡 Suggestion -->
10. The block added to `docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md` cites `cleanup-error-handling.md` for the shutdown-wait claim and then cites the same page again in the next sentence for "how cancellation unwinds", which reads as though two different pages were meant. Both statements are true. (raised by 1/4 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: the finding is about how two citations read, not about any mechanism's covered set, and rewording changes no output; searched the repository for tool consumers of this page's filename across .sh, .py, .yml, .yaml, .jq, .toml and .cfg files and found none; the page is internal documentation that nothing publishes -->
11. The profile row-cap test pins one of the three offloaded runners: `test_profile_row_cap_reaches_offloaded_runner` in `tests/unit/test_event_loop_offload.py` exercises `PostgresRunner` only, while MySQL and SQLite each gained the same `asyncio.to_thread` hop and each read `effective_row_cap` inside the thread (`src/sqllens/agent/integrations/sqlite/sql_runner.py` line 134), so switching either to `loop.run_in_executor` — the mistake all three in-code comments warn against — would silently fetch the base `max_rows` with no failing test, because the liveness tests for those runners pass either way. (raised by 1/4 agents)

</details>

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] While a `query_database` call is blocked inside a synchronous Anthropic client call or inside a synchronous database driver call (connect, execute or fetch), the event loop keeps running other tasks, and the HTTP transport answers `GET /healthz`. This holds for non-streaming and streaming Anthropic requests and for each of the Postgres, MySQL and SQLite runners.
- [ ] Two `query_database` calls with different conversation ids, each blocked inside a synchronous Anthropic or database call, are blocked at the same time: neither waits for the other call to finish before entering its own blocking call.
- [ ] Two `query_database` calls with the same conversation id do not overlap: the second call's agent run starts only after the first call has returned, failed or been cancelled. When both calls return or fail, the conversation's history afterwards holds the first call's messages followed by the second call's messages.
- [ ] After every call on a conversation has returned, failed or been cancelled — including a call cancelled while it was waiting for its turn — the server holds no per-conversation queue entry for that conversation id.
- [ ] When a `query_database` call is cancelled while it is running, the conversation holds none of the messages that call added and keeps every message that was in it when the cancelled call's turn began (after any earlier call on that conversation id finished). The next call on that conversation id runs with that history.
- [ ] When a `query_database` call is cancelled, the tool function raises the cancellation and returns no result.
- [ ] For the same conversation id, the same sequence of Anthropic responses and the same query results, a `query_database` call returns the same text content and the same `_meta` as before this change, apart from the duration values in the agent trace. This holds for both streaming and non-streaming Anthropic requests.
- [ ] An Anthropic API error raised during a call still produces an `isError: true` result, and a database error or statement timeout raised by a runner still produces a failed `run_sql` step that the agent can re-plan from, as before this change.
- [ ] A database query run under a profile whose `max_rows` is lower than the base config's fetches at most that profile's `max_rows` plus one rows from the driver.
- [ ] The change leaves these as they are: - It adds no interruption of work already running on a worker thread. A cancelled call's database query keeps running until it finishes or the engine's statement timeout stops it. Nothing but the query's own end stops it when `statement_timeout_ms = 0`, or when it is a MySQL statement other than `SELECT`, which MySQL's `MAX_EXECUTION_TIME` does not cover. A cancelled call's Anthropic request keeps running, and is billed, until it returns. Server shutdown waits for such threads. - It adds no thread pool of its own. Anthropic calls and database queries share asyncio's default executor, so beyond its thread count further calls wait for a free thread. The ChromaDB memory store keeps its own two-thread pool. - It leaves the synchronous memory-store calls of `import_memory` and the memory-administration MCP tools on the event loop, so those tools still block it while they run. - It leaves the scratch CSV write after each query, `df.to_csv`, and the read-only and row-level-security guards' SQL parsing on the event loop. - It adds no progress notifications and no acknowledge-now / fetch-later job API. A `query_database` call still holds its request open until the agent run ends, so a question that takes longer than a client's timeout still times out for that client.
- [ ] After the change: - `docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md` states that `query_database`'s Anthropic calls and database queries run on worker threads, that calls sharing a conversation id run one at a time, that a cancelled call's messages are removed from its conversation, and that `import_memory` and the memory-administration tools still block the event loop. - `docs/internal/database-connectors/cleanup-error-handling.md` and `docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md` state that a cancelled request's database query keeps running on its worker thread until it finishes or the engine's statement timeout stops it. - `docs/external/getting-started.md` states that a question waiting on the AI service or the database does not stop the server from accepting other requests, and that `import_memory` and the memory-administration tools can still briefly block them.
